previous_draft_decision.reason: Remove the optional kaq to avoid the independently attested ordinal-first construction. Direct prenominal ñawpaq has a same-Chanka previous-number example; it can modify the already lexicalized multiword draft noun. This recommendation preserves the prior temporal meaning rather than treating the internal ñawpa of draft as sufficient. The repeated roots remain, but now serve two distinct scopes. Exact full-string publication is not required; native rhythm remains uncertified, not a blanket blocker.
previous_draft_decision.limits: The original is not proved ungrammatical: the source also glosses the kaq compound as predecessor. Revision is a conservative ambiguity reduction, not a categorical claim that kaq always means first.
previous_draft_decision.ordinal_source_details: Elvia Andia Grageda, university-hosted language teaching material, ordinal-numbers section. Mixed Cusco/Ayacucho presentation; used only to establish the plausible ordinal reading, not to transfer region-specific wording.

grammar.genitive: llank'ay-pa: consonant-final possessor takes -pa; kikinchasqa-n: vowel-final lexicalized nominal copy takes third-person possessed -n. Own Cuzco syntax supports genitive + nominalized -sqa-n nouns, including picture/artifact referents.
grammar.scope: Llank'aypa ñawpa kikinchasqan makes previous apply to copy. Revised Llank'aypa manaraq waqaychasqa kikinchasqan makes not-yet-saved apply to copy. Reordering is conservative scope clarification, not proof the original could never receive the intended reading.
grammar.accusative: kikinchasqa-n-ta in restoration failure and reopening memory rows is correct possession-before-case order; own Copy Text Box supplies the same -n-ta pattern.
grammar.purpose: kutichi-na-paq and kicha-na-paq are purpose constructions; source technical memory sentence directly supports the latter. No completed-recovery or future-success guarantee.
grammar.notyet: Copy may denote the live or prospective working copy before storage. Persistence is asserted by the saved status and denied by not-yet-saved; the noun alone must not be described as inherently already persisted.

grammar_and_semantics: llank'ay-pa is a consonant-final work genitive. Herrero’s own Cochabamba ñawpaqe entry explicitly describes -pa/-paj after a non-vowel relation term and corresponding possessive suffixes. Its llank'ay sense 4 supplies work as nominal action/effect with my/your/Pedro’s-work examples. Sense 2 marks general work as especially urban/castellanized, whereas rural sense 1 concerns ploughing; this distinction is disclosed, not erased.

Own QUH software copied-document wording and nominal plural Copies support kikinchasqa as a copy noun. Vowel-final noun + possessive -n gives kikinchasqan, then accusative -ta gives kikinchasqanta. QUH Textoq tawak’uchun / tawak’uchunta directly exemplifies possessed noun and possessed object; CENAQ corroborates -n possession and -pa genitive, explicitly CHU-marked rather than Cochabamba-exclusive.

The functional work-copy wording covers arbitrary live or persisted bitmap/editing state, including imported or apparently finished artwork. It is not asserted to be a standardized one-word computer-draft term or an exact published complete GUI phrase. Saved/not-yet/restored/preserved states are supplied by each predicate or modifier, not presupposed by the copy noun.

All previous-state labels preserve temporal prior semantics with ñawpaq. No ordinal kaq is added. manaraq jallch’asqa is inside the possessed noun phrase and scopes over copy. Regional jallch’ay, ñawpaq and watiqmanta are justified independently rather than transferred mechanically from QUZ.

common_semantics: kutichi-na-paq expresses recovery/restoration purpose. It is not the completed -sqa recovery state and does not promise the archive will be recoverable. kikinchasqa-ta is an unpossessed recovery-copy object; the longer previous-working-copy sentences use llank’ay-pa ... kikinchasqa-n-ta, genitive then possessed noun then accusative.

Both own regional AbiWord files contain the nonfuzzy computer Export File entry Jawaman khiputa apachiy. This is direct software-export evidence, not a deduction solely from postal send. In AN Paint this can write a selected local/provider URI and is not intrinsically network sending.

QUH jawaman is retained. QUZ hawaman is a transparent own-variety spelling/composition choice: AMLQ hawa includes outside/exterior, and its man entry explicitly gives directional-to usage and examples, despite calling the suffix ablative in a loose grammatical label. APL/Calvo EX- entry independently prints exterior hawaman. Not a blanket mechanical j-to-h replacement.

The separate-preservation branch attempts to retain one intact ZIP independently from replacement autosave. Multiple historic copies may exist, but this failure message is about the single prior draft; no divided archive fragments or distributed content are involved.

QUH and QUZ separation choices are independently grounded. QUH t’aqasqata has directly attested nonmixed/planned-separation manner semantics. QUZ original t’aqa t’aqa is not categorically declared ungrammatical, but the narrower non-distributive sapaq revision is preferable on available own-variety evidence.
